question: Asked to place one million on a line running from one thousand to one billion, where do many people put it?
answer: Near the middle. In Landy and colleagues' 2013 study, many adults placed a million roughly halfway, as if thousand, million and billion came in equal steps. In fact a million sits a thousandth of the way along, almost touching the start. Two words that differ by one letter hide a thousandfold gap.
move: Put big numbers on one scale before judging how far apart they are.
ask: When two numbers sound alike, have I checked how far apart they really are?
reference: Landy, Silbert & Goldin, Estimating large numbers, Cognitive Science 37:775–799, 2013
